name: Chia Hung Hsiao
about:
I am a master’s student at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, studying Artificial Intelligence Innovation in the VLSI Signal Processing Lab. My work explores efficient AI hardware, reduced-precision computing, and digital circuit design.

I enjoy translating algorithms into practical hardware—from systolic-array architectures to FPGA signal processing.
interests: AI accelerators, Digital IC design, FPGA, Signal processing

experience.description:
Developed 32 × 8 complex matrix multiplication with phase using CORDIC algorithms and fixed-point arithmetic to reduce multiplier and memory usage.
Designed a CDMA-based transceiver integrating Kasami, Gold, and Walsh PN codes into DSSS; evaluated BER and interference performance across SNR levels in an AWGN channel.

projects.title: Reduced-Precision AI Accelerator
projects.subtitle: RTL · Synthesis · PyTorch
projects.description: Designed a low-cost AI accelerator based on Google’s TPU with weight compensation. The proposed systolic array reduced overall hardware overhead by 16.64%, while improving accuracy by 0.1–0.6% compared with INT8 quantization.

projects.title: CORDIC Algorithm & Applications
projects.subtitle: Verilog · Fixed-point arithmetic
projects.description: Designed hardware-efficient RTL for approximate sine and cosine computation with absolute error ≤ 0.00025. Extended CORDIC to approximate decimal multiplication.
